text: All the people gathered together in the square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had given Israel.
So on the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly of men, women, and all who could listen with understanding.

He read out of it facing the square in front of the Water Gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men, the women, and those who could understand. All the people listened attentively to the Book of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a high wooden platform built for this purpose. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, and on his left, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book in full view of all the people, since he was elevated above them, and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
Ezra praised the LORD, the great God, and all the people lifted their hands and answered, Amen, Amen. Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

The Levites — Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah — helped the people understand the Law while everyone remained standing in their places.
They read plainly from the Book of the Law of God, giving the meaning so that the people could understand what was read.

Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to them all, This day is holy to the LORD your God; do not mourn or weep. For all the people were weeping as they listened to the words of the Law.

Then Nehemiah said, Go and eat rich food, drink sweet wine, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
The Levites quieted the people, saying, Be still, for the day is holy; do not grieve.
So all the people went away to eat and drink, to send portions to others, and to celebrate with great joy, because they had understood what had been read to them.
On the second day, the family heads of all the people, along with the priests and Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law more closely.
They found written in the Law that the LORD had commanded through Moses that the Israelites should live in shelters during the festival of the seventh month,

and that they should announce this message in all their towns and in Jerusalem: Go out to the hill country and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees to make shelters, as it is written.

So the people went out, gathered branches, and built shelters — on their own rooftops, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of God's house, and in the squares at the Water Gate and the Ephraim Gate.

The whole assembly of those who had returned from exile built shelters and lived in them. The Israelites had not celebrated this way since the days of Joshua son of Nun, and there was very great rejoicing.
Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God every day, from the first day to the last. They kept the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a closing assembly, as required.
